$comment: GENERATED by tools/desk-registry.py — never hand-edited, and checks.py fails when it is stale. It is the slot registry the hosted Media Desk serves, because a serverless function cannot import tools/lib or read data/. It carries no photograph state: the desk reads the register live, so a photograph acquired an hour ago shows as filled without a rebuild. The provider verdicts ARE generated, from acquire.cleared(), because they change with a commit rather than with an acquisition — and they are not the gate: acquire.py refuses inside the workflow, where the key is. A TEMPLATED ROW CARRIES NO REQUIREMENTS: they are the SLOT's, stated once under `slots`, because 590 copies of the same 300-word brief is half a megabyte saying one thing, and a value repeated 590 times is 590 places for it to differ.

unsplash.because: unsplash: REFUSED for automated acquisition. The provider's own words: "All API uses must use the hotlinked image URLs returned by the API under the `photo.urls`  properties. This applies to all uses of the image and not just search results." — The architecture required here is acquire through the API and then self-host. This sentence forbids the second half for anything the API returns, and "all uses of the image and not just search results" closes the reading that it covers previews only. The two halves are not separable, so the answer is no rather than yes-with-conditions. A second clause points the same way and is recorded although the outcome does not turn on it: "The API is to be used for non-automated, high-quality, and authentic experiences." The article explaining that phrase is not archived and not read, which is why it is not the reason. Unsplash's LICENCE route — a photograph obtained without the API — is unaffected and is not this architecture. This script is the automated path; it does not have a manual mode and must not grow one.

category-hero.note: One of the eight discovery categories, each with its own photographic language: Nature is forest, water and wildlife; Adventure is a body doing something; Food is hands and produce rather than a plated dish. The category page is 4,980 pixels of one row shape and reads as a tourism database — docs/signature-moments.md refuses a MAP here and records why, and records that the thinness is a licence position rather than a design one. This is the answer to it.

country-hero.note: What a whole country feels like, above its name. Never a single famous landmark and never a city skyline: a landmark is a place INSIDE the country and the capital has its own role. Fifty of these are seen one after another by a reader moving through /countries, so the SET is part of the brief exactly as it is for the four doors — different light, different season and different palette between neighbours. THE BAND IS AN ADDITION AND NOT A REPLACEMENT: the country portrait stays exactly where it is, because it is this family's signature moment and it is the thing that says which country the page is about. With no photograph there is no band at all, which is today's page unchanged — a slot waiting for a picture is honest and three hundred pixels of it is a hole.

destination-hero.note: A destination portrait has to say what it is like to BE there — the valley floor against the wall above it, the water the town turns towards. Never a monument alone and never an aerial: the page already draws where the place is, four hundred pixels above this, so a photograph that answers 'where' duplicates the map.

interest-hero.note: What this way of travelling LOOKS like, being done. Seventeen of these are seen against each other by a reader moving through /interests, so the set is part of the brief: Mountains and Coast must not both be a view from a summit. The page draws its own tag across Europe under this, which answers where; the photograph answers what it is like.

journey-hero.note: The journey's own atmosphere rather than any one of its stops: movement, or the landscape changing, or the reward at the end. A journey page draws its route four hundred pixels below this, so a photograph answering WHERE would duplicate the map. THE FIVE-STAGE SEQUENCE — departure, movement, transition, arrival, reward — is not this slot: it is five photographs per journey and needs five containers, which is a composition nobody has designed. This is the one that says what the trip feels like.

macro-hero.note: A continental quarter in one frame: the ground five countries share. The Nordics is long light and folded coast; Iberia is dry upland and terraced hill. Nine of these and they are the widest claim any photograph on this site makes, so no single landmark and no single country may stand for the group.

place-hero.note: A place is one thing inside a destination — a bridge, a cellar, a cable car — so this is the closest frame the site has. It must be that thing and not the town around it: the destination page one level up already carries the wider picture, and a page that shows the same view as its parent has said nothing. Without a photograph this container draws a minimap, so a picture here REPLACES geography and has to earn it.

region-hero.note: What distinguishes this region from the others in its country. NEVER THE COUNTRY'S OWN PICTURE: Provence is not France and Brittany is not France, and a region page that reuses the country photograph says they are. The material a region is made of — its stone, its roofs, its crop, its water — so a reader who knows the country can say which region this is without the caption. 130 of these, the second-largest family on the site.

story-hero.note: A human moment that could be the opening frame of this particular long read — not a landmark, and not a generic European scene that would serve any of the nine. Without a photograph this container draws the story's own places on the atlas, which is a real claim about the piece, so a photograph here replaces something honest and has to be better than it. A STORY IS NOT A PLACE: its picture may never be drawn from a hash, which is the rule this container exists to hold.

theme-hero.note: A theme is an ARGUMENT about Europe rather than a place in it — Medieval Europe, Thermal Europe — so the photograph is the argument's subject caught once: a guild square, a bathhouse, a painted ceiling. The page draws the theme's eight stops as a constellation beneath, which is the reach; this is the substance.

purposes.surface: The opening of the atlas index — a wide editorial image beside the headline.
purposes.note: One country seen whole from the ground: a valley, a coast or a plain with enough of it in frame that the eye reads a country rather than a spot. Never an aerial, never a flag, never a monument, and never a composite of several places — the page's argument is that Europe is fifty separate countries, and a picture that could be anywhere argues the opposite. The drawing it replaces is the fifty drawn as fifty, so a photograph has to be at least as specific as that. These open the indexes on the menu bar and are seen in sequence by anyone walking it, so a set that reads as one stock search fails even when each passes alone. A count typed here is the count that was true before the next index got an opening.

purposes.surface: The Coast & islands door on the homepage — a large editorial card under “Find your Europe”.
purposes.note: Where land ends. A cliff, a harbour or an island shore with the sea doing the work. These four sit side by side, so a set that reads as four photographs from one stock search fails the brief even when each one passes on its own.

purposes.surface: The Food & wine door on the homepage — a large editorial card under “Find your Europe”.
purposes.note: A table, a market or a vineyard that could only be where it is. Never a styled plate on a board. These four sit side by side, so a set that reads as four photographs from one stock search fails the brief even when each one passes on its own.

purposes.surface: The Historic cities door on the homepage — a large editorial card under “Find your Europe”.
purposes.note: A lived-in old street, not a monument. Somebody's Tuesday in a two-thousand-year-old city. These four sit side by side, so a set that reads as four photographs from one stock search fails the brief even when each one passes on its own.

purposes.surface: The Mountains door on the homepage — a large editorial card under “Find your Europe”.
purposes.note: An alpine morning above cloud — a valley floor against the wall over it, not a summit portrait. These four sit side by side, so a set that reads as four photographs from one stock search fails the brief even when each one passes on its own.

purposes.surface: The opening of the events index.
purposes.note: A European gathering in progress — a procession, a market, a festival crowd at dusk. It must read as a fixture in a real town, not a stadium. These open the indexes on the menu bar and are seen in sequence by anyone walking it, so a set that reads as one stock search fails even when each passes alone. A count typed here is the count that was true before the next index got an opening.

purposes.surface: The opening of the experiences index.
purposes.note: Somebody DOING the thing — hands, a workshop, a kitchen, a boat. A person at work in a real place, not a posed portrait and not an empty interior. These open the indexes on the menu bar and are seen in sequence by anyone walking it, so a set that reads as one stock search fails even when each passes alone. A count typed here is the count that was true before the next index got an opening.

purposes.surface: The full-bleed opening of the homepage, with the masthead over it and the headline beside it.
purposes.note: docs/hero-brief.md holds the editorial brief. The plate system was MEASURED as unable to carry this surface, which is the whole argument for licensing a photograph at all — so a photograph that reads as generic stock fails the brief even when it passes every number here. THE FLOOR WAS 1.6 AND IT REFUSED FIFTEEN OF FIFTEEN. Every landscape result of the first real search measured 1.50, which is 3:2, the native aspect of essentially every camera a stock photographer owns — so the one purpose on this site that asked for 1.6 was asking for a crop rather than a photograph, and refused the whole library. It was also backwards for its own brief: the brief wants a strong 21:9 desktop crop AND a viable portrait crop out of the SAME frame, and a narrower source has more room for both, not less. Cropping 3:2 to 21:9 keeps 64% of the height; cropping 2.6:1 to 3:4 keeps 29% of the width. 1.5 is what every other purpose here already asks for. AND THE CEILING WAS 2.6, WHICH WAS THE SAME MISTAKE AT THE OTHER END. The container this sits in was measured for the first time and swings 0.435 to 2.326 — at 320x900 the block is a tall portrait and at a wide desktop it is a band. A 2.6:1 source in a 0.435 container shows 17% of its own width, so the ceiling admitted a shape that cannot survive the narrow end AND that, by this file's own note, essentially no stock photographer supplies. 1.9 costs nothing real and takes the guaranteed frame from 11% to 15%.

purposes.surface: The opening of the journeys index — a wide editorial image beside the headline.
purposes.note: A road, a rail line or a pass with distance in it: the feeling of crossing a border on purpose. Never a map, and never a single landmark. These open the indexes on the menu bar and are seen in sequence by anyone walking it, so a set that reads as one stock search fails even when each passes alone. A count typed here is the count that was true before the next index got an opening.

purposes.surface: The opening of the stories index.
purposes.note: A human moment that could be the opening frame of a long read. Faces are welcome; a landmark is not. These open the indexes on the menu bar and are seen in sequence by anyone walking it, so a set that reads as one stock search fails even when each passes alone. A count typed here is the count that was true before the next index got an opening.
